summary: Administrative, physical and technical safeguards to ensure confidentiality, integrity and availability of ePHI; risk-based and scalable (164.306(b)).
applies_to: HIPAA covered entities (health plans, clearinghouses, providers that conduct standard electronic transactions) and their business associates.
size_thresholds: No size exemption; 164.306(b)(2) lets entities factor size, complexity, capabilities and cost when choosing measures.
status: In force; eCFR text current as of 2026-09-23 unchanged by the Jan 2025 NPRM (see separate entry).

summary: Limits uses/disclosures of PHI, minimum necessary, individual rights, BAAs, and administrative safeguards (164.530(c)).
applies_to: HIPAA covered entities and business associates.
size_thresholds: Covered entity status turns on function, not size. 'Small health plan' = annual receipts of $5M or less (160.103; relevant to historical compliance timing only). A group health plan with fewer than 50 participants that is self-administered by the employer is not a 'group health plan' under 160.103.
status: In force. The eCFR still shows the 2024 reproductive health care amendments (164.502(a)(5)(iii)); a federal court reportedly vacated them in June 2025. That status is not confirmed from a .gov source here.

summary: Notify individuals, HHS and (for more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction) prominent media after a breach of unsecured PHI; business associates notify the covered entity.
size_thresholds: Media notice only when more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction are affected. HHS notice is contemporaneous for 500 or more; fewer than 500 goes in an annual log due within 60 days after calendar year end.

summary: Proposed overhaul: remove required/addressable distinction, mandate written asset inventory/network map, encryption, MFA, annual compliance audits, restore critical systems within 72 hours.
applies_to: Covered entities and business associates (if finalized).
status: PROPOSED ONLY. Comments closed 2025-03-07. No final rule in the Federal Register as of 2026-09-25. Fall 2025 Unified Agenda lists it as a Long-Term Action with Final Action 07/2027.

summary: Confidentiality of substance use disorder treatment records. 2024 rule aligns with HIPAA (single TPO consent) and 2.16 requires formal security policies for paper and electronic records. 2.16(b) applies HIPAA breach notification to Part 2 records.
applies_to: Federally assisted Part 2 programs and lawful holders of Part 2 records.
size_thresholds: No size threshold (2.16(a)(2) exempts family/friends and other informal caregivers).
status: Final rule 89 FR 12472 (Feb 16, 2024), effective Apr 16, 2024; compliance date Feb 16, 2026. 2.25 accounting of disclosures is tolled pending a HIPAA 164.528 revision.

summary: Vendors of personal health records (incl. health apps) and PHR-related entities must notify individuals, the FTC and (for 500 or more residents) media of breaches of unsecured PHR identifiable health information, including unauthorized disclosures.
applies_to: Vendors of PHRs, PHR-related entities and third-party service providers NOT covered by HIPAA (318.1 excludes covered entities and business associates acting as such).
size_thresholds: FTC notice is contemporaneous (within 60 days) for 500 or more individuals; fewer than 500 may be logged and reported annually within 60 days after year end. Media notice for 500 or more residents of a state.

short_name: Section 1557 - Patient care decision support tools
summary: Covered entities must not discriminate through patient care decision support tools (including AI/algorithms): ongoing reasonable efforts to identify tools using race, color, national origin, sex, age or disability inputs, and to mitigate discrimination risk.
applies_to: Recipients of HHS federal financial assistance operating health programs (hospitals, clinics, providers taking Medicare Part A/Medicaid, etc.), HHS programs and ACA Title I entities.
status: 92.210(a) effective July 5, 2024; (b) and (c) compliance within 300 days (by May 1, 2025) per 92.1(b). A June 2, 2026 HHS notice (91 FR 32887) reports vacatur only of gender-identity provisions (Tennessee v. Kennedy, S.D. Miss., Oct 22, 2025). Other provisions, including 92.210, remain in force.

citation: 42 CFR 482.15 (hospitals; parallel rules for 16 other provider types)
summary: All-hazards risk assessment, emergency plan reviewed at least every 2 years, policies and procedures, communication plan, training and testing. Covers resilience to IT/cyber outages.
applies_to: Medicare/Medicaid-participating hospitals (482.15) and other certified provider/supplier types.

summary: Social assistance organizations (NAICS 624: child/family services, community food/housing, vocational rehab, child day care) are HIPAA covered entities ONLY if they are health plans or clearinghouses, or furnish health care AND transmit health information electronically in HIPAA standard transactions (e.g., billing Medicaid electronically). Otherwise HIPAA does not apply, though state law, program rules (45 CFR 205.50, 42 CFR 431.300) and contracts (BAAs) often do.
